investigacion.base:
**Bottom line:** Based on current reporting, this would resolve **No**. Israeli forces are moving *past* the original Yellow Line into Gaza, not pulling back behind it. No announced or actual pullback has been reported.

**What the cited sources say**
- **OCHA situation report (26 June 2026) and Metaculus Q45860:** I couldn't open either page directly. The Metaculus question opened on 12 Oct 2026. Its question text defines the line as the October 2025 ceasefire map and says the "Orange Lines" don't matter.
- **Metaculus FAQ:** "Credible sources" generally means reputable media or official reporting.
- **What would count as Yes:** Israel must both announce a pullback and physically leave the area, so it no longer controls it, for at least 24 hours. A partial pullback that still leaves troops ahead of the original line probably would not count.

**Background**
- **Oct 2025 ceasefire:** The line was based on a map Trump posted on 4 Oct 2025, which was expected to leave about 58% of Gaza under Israeli control.  Israeli forces pulled back to it around 10 Oct 2025. 
- **11 Jan 2026:** Satellite images showed Israeli forces had moved the yellow concrete blocks hundreds of metres past the line, further into Gaza. 
- **14 Jan 2026:** The US said phase two of the ceasefire was starting, but gave no timeline for the next withdrawal. That withdrawal is tied to Hamas disarming. 
- **4 Aug 2026:** After Trump announced a deal in late July, the US-led Board of Peace said Israel would pull back past the Yellow Line "only once decommissioning is complete." 
- **Disarmament deadlock:** Israel says it "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed." Hamas will only disarm step by step alongside Israeli pullbacks. 

**Most recent news**
- **11 Oct 2026:** Israeli forces moved the blocks further west in Shujayea, Gaza City, taking more of the neighbourhood and forcing families to flee. 
- **13 Oct 2026:** Israel now controls about 65% of Gaza according to the UN, up from the 53% agreed a year ago. 

**How often has this happened?**
- In about 12 months of ceasefire, Israel has pulled back once (the initial pullback in Oct 2025). Since then it has never moved back behind the line and has repeatedly moved forward. That makes the chance of a Yes in the roughly 2.5 months left low.

**Possible triggers before 1 Jan 2027**
- I found no scheduled withdrawal date.
- The only clear route to Yes is Hamas completing disarmament, verified by the Board of Peace and mediators, followed by an Israeli pullback. Heavy US pressure could also force a move.
- Watch for Board of Peace announcements and any news on Hamas disarmament.

I didn't find any prediction-market prices for this question.

criterios: This question resolves as **Yes** if, at any point before 1 January 2027, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) report that Israeli military forces have announced a withdrawal to a position behind the Yellow Line within Gaza (as defined by the specific map drawn up for the October 2025 ceasefire agreement, illustrated by [the OCHA](https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-report-26-june-2026#access-restricted-areas)) and that Israeli military forces have physically withdrawn to such a position that they no longer maintain military control of the area vacated.
letra_pequena:
Any distance behind the Yellow Line will qualify so long as it is announced and maintained for a minimum of a 24-hour period.

The status of the "Orange Lines" is irrelevant to this question.

razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 77 days, from 16 October to 1 January 2027.

(b) **Status quo:** No. Israeli forces reportedly control more territory than they did at the original Yellow Line.

(c) **Reference class:** In roughly a year since the October 2025 ceasefire, there have been no reported, announced withdrawals *behind the original line*. That is a narrow historical base rate, but it supports a low near-term probability.

(d) **No scenario:** The disarmament impasse persists, and Israeli forces remain at or beyond the original line through December.

(e) **Yes scenario:** A negotiated step or strong outside pressure leads Israel to announce and carry out a pullback behind the original line before the deadline.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** The pullback need not cover all of Gaza or last indefinitely. Any announced withdrawal behind the *original* line qualifies if Israel relinquishes military control of the vacated area for at least 24 hours. Merely moving the line’s markers would not qualify.

Probability: 7%

(a) **Time left:** about 2.5 months, from 16 Oct 2026 to the 1 Jan 2027 deadline.

(b) **Status quo:** No. Israel is not withdrawing. It is moving the line further into Gaza. It now controls about 65% of the Strip, up from the 53% set in the October 2025 agreement. The latest move came in Shujayea on 11 Oct 2026.

(c) **Reference class and base rate:**
- In 12 months of ceasefire, there has been one pullback. That was the initial move to the Yellow Line in Oct 2025.
- There have been zero pullbacks behind the line, and the line has advanced repeatedly since.
- In stalled ceasefires that make withdrawal conditional on disarmament, further phased withdrawals within short windows are rare.
- The base rate for a qualifying withdrawal in any given 2.5-month window is well under 5%.

(d) **No scenario:** Hamas disarmament stays deadlocked. Israel says there will be no withdrawal before full disarmament, and the Board of Peace backs that. The Yellow Line keeps creeping west, and the year ends with Israel still holding more than 53% of Gaza.

(e) **Yes scenario:** A sudden breakthrough happens. Hamas hands over weapons in a verified way under the Board of Peace mechanism, or heavy US pressure from Trump forces a move. Israel then announces a pullback from the Yellow Line to a deeper perimeter and physically vacates territory for at least 24 hours before 1 Jan 2027.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- Israel must both announce the withdrawal and physically leave the area so it no longer controls it.
- The withdrawal must go behind the *original* October 2025 line. Simply reversing recent encroachments back to the original line would not count, since Israel would still hold about 53%.
- Orange Lines are irrelevant.
- So even a partial de-escalation, such as returning moved blocks, very likely resolves No.

Given the clear trend of advance, the explicit condition that disarmament must come first, the absence of any scheduled withdrawal, and the short window, the probability is very low.

Probability: 2%

(a) **Time left:** About 77 days, until 1 January 2027.  
(b) **Status quo:** No. Israeli forces remain beyond the original Yellow Line, and no qualifying withdrawal has been announced.  
(c) **Reference class:** In the roughly 12 months since the initial October 2025 pullback, the reported rate of further withdrawals behind the original line is **zero**. That is a small sample, but it supports a low near-term probability.  
(d) **No scenario:** The disarmament deadlock persists, and Israel maintains or expands its current positions.  
(e) **Yes scenario:** A diplomatic agreement or change in Israeli policy produces an announced pullback that is carried out before year-end.  
(f) **Resolution technicality:** A complete withdrawal from Gaza is unnecessary. Any distance behind the *original* Yellow Line can qualify, but the announcement must be followed by a physical withdrawal that ends Israeli military control of the vacated area for at least 24 hours. Moving only behind a later, shifted line would not suffice.

**Probability: 5%**
